summary: Kin Cheung works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo, attested in 2017.
King Chung Lo specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Leipzig University under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco in 2009.
King Pong Chiu specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under doctoral supervisor Jacqueline Suthren Hirst, attested in 2014.

Kirby Flower Smith (1862–1918) studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve, Minton Warren, and Maurice Bloomfield. He was a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and Director of the American Academy in Rome (1914–1915).
Kisari Mohan Ganguli (1848–1908) worked in the field of Indology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.
Kisho Masanobu (born 1950) specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a master's course at Kyoto University (~1973–1975) and served as a part-time lecturer there around 1987.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under traditional teachers including Madhusudana Nyāyācārya, Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha, Narmada Tarkatirtha, Panchanana Sastri, and Narayana Chandra Gosvami Nyāyācārya, as well as Gopinath Bhattacharya and Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya, holding a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitaro Nishida (1870–1945) studied under Tokiyuki Hojo and Karl Florenz at the University of Tokyo. Active in philosophy and religious studies, he taught at the Fourth Higher School and was Professor of Philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928).

Kiyoaki Okuda (born 1938) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1970–1973) and held posts at International Buddhist University (attested 1993) and as director of Shitennoji Kyogaku Kenkyujo (attested 2000).

Kiyoshi Kato (1907–1956) studied Tibetology and Buddhist studies at Otani University under Enga Teramoto, earning a BA in 1931. He held posts at Higashi Honganji (1935) and Kojo Girls' Vocational School (1938).
Kiyoshi Miki (1897–1945) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida (~1917–1920). He later held posts at Otani University (~1924–1927) and Ryukoku University.

Kiyoshi Okano (born 1957) works in Indology and Buddhist studies, having studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. At Kyushu University, he served as associate professor (attested 2002) and professor (attested 2013–2024).

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe works in Buddhist studies and completed a doctoral program at Rissho University. He served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 2001) and special researcher at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).

Kiyoshi Yabuuchi (1906–2000) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929) and subsequently held academic posts at Kyoto University (~1937–1969) and Ryukoku University (~1969–1979).

Kiyotaka Kimura (born 1940) studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo. A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, he held posts at the University of Tokyo (1983–2001) and served as President of Tsurumi University (~2003–2011).

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu (born 1958) works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer, later holding posts at Hokkaido University (~1993–2004), Tohoku University (~2004–2023), and Toyo Bunko.

Kiyozo Kazama (born 1928) studied linguistics and Indology at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Kōzu, and at the University of Vienna. He held professorial posts at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo, and Hosei University.

Klaus Bruhn (1928–2016) was an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf and Walther Schubring. He served as Professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1991.

Klaus Butzenberger (born 1964) studied at the University of Munich under Friedrich Wilhelm and habilitated at the Free University of Berlin. Active in Indology and philosophy, he succeeded Heinrich von Stietencron as chairholder at the University of Tübingen (1999–2017).

Klaus Karttunen (born 1951) earned his degrees through PhD at the University of Helsinki under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola. In Indology and history/archaeology, he held posts at the University of Helsinki and the Academy of Finland.
